name: Aditya-L1
tagline: A watchful eye on the Sun, stationed where a delicate gravitational balance gives it an uninterrupted view.
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Study the Sun’s photosphere, chromosphere and corona, along with solar wind particles and magnetic fields, from a halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L1 point.
beats.achieved: Aditya-L1 was inserted into its targeted halo orbit on January 6, 2024. ISRO has released scientific datasets covering solar atmospheric and in-situ measurements.
beats.ending: The mission has not ended. It requires periodic orbit maintenance and continues its solar observation programme.
beats.now: ISRO lists Aditya-L1 as operational. Its data are made available to researchers through India’s space science data infrastructure.
beats.learned: The mission strengthens India’s ability to study space weather and understand solar activity that can affect satellites, communications and power systems.

sources.label: ISRO: Aditya-L1 first halo orbit completion
